name: clinisource_clinical_gold_v1
description: Curated multi-textbook clinical & anatomical evaluation benchmark grounded against Harrison 22e, Williams Endocrinology 15e, Cornea 5e, and Anatomy & Physiology 2e.

cases.query: What is the initial biochemical diagnostic workup and case detection criteria for suspected pheochromocytoma?
expected_answer_points: Plasma free metanephrines or 24-hour urinary fractionated metanephrines are first-line diagnostic tests
Clinical suspicion includes hyperadrenergic spells, resistant hypertension, or incidental adrenal mass
Localization imaging (CT/MRI) follows biochemical confirmation
cases.notes: Verified in Williams Ch 14 Endocrine Hypertension (p. 683-689).

cases.query: How is primary aldosteronism screened and diagnosed using plasma aldosterone concentration and renin activity?
expected_answer_points: Plasma aldosterone concentration (PAC) to plasma renin activity (PRA) ratio (ARR) is the primary screening test
Suppressed renin with elevated aldosterone characterizes primary aldosteronism

Confirmatory testing (e.g., oral sodium loading, saline infusion, fludrocortisone suppression, or captopril challenge) is required unless spontaneous hypokalemia with undetectable renin and marked PAC elevation
cases.notes: Verified in Williams Ch 14 Primary Aldosteronism (p. 692-694, Fig 14.9).

cases.query: Explain the steps of thyroid hormone synthesis including iodide trapping, organification, and coupling in thyroid follicular cells.
expected_answer_points: Active iodide uptake via the sodium-iodide symporter (NIS) across the basolateral membrane
Oxidation and organification of iodide onto thyroglobulin tyrosine residues catalyzed by thyroid peroxidase (TPO)
Coupling of MIT and DIT to yield T3 and T4 regulated by TSH
cases.notes: Verified in Williams Ch 9 Thyroid Pathophysiology (p. 415-420, Fig 9.1).

cases.query: What are the first-line screening tests to confirm endogenous hypercortisolism in suspected Cushing syndrome?
expected_answer_points: Low-dose overnight dexamethasone suppression test (1 mg)
Late-night salivary cortisol measuring loss of circadian nadir
24-hour urinary free cortisol (UFC) excretion
cases.notes: Verified in Williams Ch 13 The Adrenal Cortex (p. 624).

cases.query: What are the diagnostic criteria and core management pillars for Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA)?
expected_answer_points: Hyperglycemia, ketonemia (beta-hydroxybutyrate >= 3 mmol/L or ketonuria), and metabolic acidosis
Immediate intravenous fluid resuscitation followed by continuous insulin therapy
Careful serum potassium monitoring and replacement before/during insulin administration
cases.notes: Verified in Williams Ch 35 Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (p. 1807).

cases.query: Explain the functional zonation of the adrenal cortex and the steroid hormones produced in each zone.
expected_answer_points: Zona glomerulosa (outer) synthesizes mineralocorticoids (aldosterone)
Zona fasciculata (middle) synthesizes glucocorticoids (cortisol)
Zona reticularis (inner) synthesizes adrenal androgens (DHEA/DHEAS)
cases.notes: Verified in Williams Ch 13 (13 chunks contain zona glomerulosa).

cases.query: How are sepsis and septic shock defined clinically, and what organ dysfunction indicators are assessed?
expected_answer_points: Sepsis is life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection
SOFA / qSOFA criteria assess respiratory, cardiovascular, hepatic, coagulation, renal, and neurologic dysfunction
Septic shock involves persistent hypotension requiring vasopressors and elevated serum lactate despite adequate fluid resuscitation
cases.notes: Verified in Harrison Ch 315 Sepsis and Septic Shock (p. 2359).

cases.query: What are the KDIGO staging criteria for Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) based on serum creatinine and urine output?
expected_answer_points: Stage 1: serum creatinine 1.5-1.9x baseline or >= 0.3 mg/dL increase, or urine output < 0.5 mL/kg/h for 6-12 hours
Stage 2: serum creatinine 2.0-2.9x baseline or urine output < 0.5 mL/kg/h for >= 12 hours
Stage 3: serum creatinine >= 3.0x baseline or >= 4.0 mg/dL or RRT initiation, or urine output < 0.3 mL/kg/h for >= 24 hours / anuria >= 12 hours
cases.notes: Verified in Harrison (12 chunks contain KDIGO).

cases.query: How do you differentiate PTH-mediated from non-PTH-mediated causes of hypercalcemia?
expected_answer_points: Elevated or inappropriately normal intact PTH indicates PTH-mediated hypercalcemia (primarily primary hyperparathyroidism)
Suppressed PTH indicates non-PTH-mediated hypercalcemia, most commonly malignancy (PTHrP or osteolytic metastases)
Other non-PTH causes include vitamin D intoxication, granulomatous disease, and thiazide/milk-alkali effects
cases.notes: Verified in Harrison Ch 57 & Ch 422 (p. 405, 3314).

cases.query: Compare the ECG and cardiac troponin diagnostic criteria distinguishing NSTEMI from unstable angina and STEMI.
expected_answer_points: Elevated cardiac troponin above the 99th percentile with rise/fall defines acute myocardial injury/infarction
STEMI features persistent ST-segment elevation or new LBBB/ischemic equivalent requiring immediate reperfusion
Unstable angina presents with ischemic symptoms without troponin elevation, whereas NSTEMI has troponin elevation without persistent ST elevation
cases.notes: Verified in Harrison Ch 285 & Ch 286 (p. 2149-2156).

cases.query: What are the primary pathogens and empiric outpatient versus inpatient antibiotic considerations for community-acquired pneumonia?
expected_answer_points: Streptococcus pneumoniae and atypical organisms (Mycoplasma, Chlamydophila, Legionella) are key etiologies
Severity scores (CURB-65 / PSI) guide outpatient vs inpatient disposition
Empiric regimens balance beta-lactams plus macrolide/doxycycline or respiratory fluoroquinolones based on comorbidities and setting
cases.notes: Verified in Harrison Ch 131 Pneumonia (p. 1066+).

cases.query: How is heart failure classified by left ventricular ejection fraction (HFrEF vs HFmrEF vs HFpEF) and what biomarkers aid diagnosis?
expected_answer_points: HFrEF is defined by LVEF <= 40%, HFmrEF by 41-49%, and HFpEF by >= 50%
BNP and NT-proBNP support diagnosis and risk stratification
Transthoracic echocardiography is essential to assess ventricular function and structural pathology
cases.notes: Verified in Harrison Ch 264 Heart Failure (p. 2018+).

cases.query: What are the major risk factors, common causative organisms (such as Pseudomonas), and diagnostic evaluation of bacterial keratitis?
expected_answer_points: Contact lens wear is a major risk factor, strongly associated with Pseudomonas aeruginosa
Other common organisms include Staphylococcus aureus, coagulase-negative staphylococci, and Streptococcus pneumoniae
Corneal scraping for Gram stain and culture precedes broad-spectrum fortified or fluoroquinolone topical antibiotics
cases.notes: Verified in Cornea Ch 20 & Ch 76 (p. 275, 863).

cases.query: Describe the pathophysiology, clinical slit-lamp findings (guttae), and surgical management options for Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy.
expected_answer_points: Progressive loss of corneal endothelial cells with Descemet membrane excrescences (cornea guttae)
Leads to corneal stromal and epithelial edema with morning visual blurring
Definitive surgical treatment includes endothelial keratoplasty (DSEK/DMEK)
cases.notes: Verified in Cornea Ch 72 (48 chunks mention guttae).

cases.query: How do epithelial (dendritic) and stromal manifestations of herpes simplex keratitis differ clinically and in management?
expected_answer_points: Epithelial HSV keratitis presents with classic branching dendritic ulcers with terminal bulbs staining with fluorescein
Epithelial keratitis is treated with topical or oral antivirals while topical corticosteroids are contraindicated
Stromal keratitis is immune-mediated and requires topical corticosteroids covered by antiviral prophylaxis
cases.notes: Verified in Cornea Ch 78 (118 chunks mention dendritic).

cases.query: What corneal topography features characterize keratoconus, and why is refractive laser ablation (LASIK) contraindicated?
expected_answer_points: Inferior steepening, asymmetric bow-tie pattern, and corneal thinning on topography/tomography
LASIK and surface ablation are contraindicated due to risk of rapid ectasia progression
Corneal collagen cross-linking (CXL) stabilizes progressive ectasia
cases.notes: Verified in Cornea Ch 11 & Ch 174 (p. 176, 1737).

cases.query: What are the key risk factors, clinical signs, and management of corneal allograft rejection following penetrating keratoplasty?
expected_answer_points: Risk factors include corneal neovascularization, prior graft rejection, and ocular inflammation
Signs include keratic precipitates, endothelial rejection line (Khodadoust line), stromal edema, and anterior chamber reaction
Prompt intensive topical corticosteroid therapy is critical to reverse rejection
cases.notes: Verified in Cornea Ch 115 (p. 1262-1267).

cases.query: Describe the anatomical pathway and sequence of the cardiac electrical conduction system from the SA node to the Purkinje fibers.
expected_answer_points: Impulse originates at the sinoatrial (SA) node in the superior right atrial wall
Travels via internodal pathways to the atrioventricular (AV) node where conduction delays briefly
Proceeds through the AV bundle (bundle of His), right and left bundle branches, and subendocardial Purkinje fibers
cases.notes: Verified in Anatomy & Physiology 2e Ch 19.2 (p. 812, Fig 19.18).

cases.query: Explain the structural components of the nephron and how hydrostatic and osmotic pressures govern glomerular filtration.
expected_answer_points: The renal corpuscle consists of the glomerulus capillary tuft surrounded by Bowman's capsule
Tubular segments include the proximal convoluted tubule, loop of Henle, distal convoluted tubule, and collecting duct
Glomerular filtration rate (GFR) depends on net filtration pressure balancing glomerular hydrostatic pressure against capsular hydrostatic and blood colloid osmotic pressures
cases.notes: Verified in Anatomy & Physiology 2e Ch 25.4 & 25.5 (p. 1165-1170, Fig 25.13).

cases.query: Describe the major spinal nerve plexuses of the body, including the organization and innervation of the brachial plexus.
expected_answer_points: Four main nerve plexuses: cervical, brachial, lumbar, and sacral
Brachial plexus arises from spinal nerves C4/C5 through T1 to innervate the upper limb
Major terminal branches include axillary, radial, median, ulnar, and musculocutaneous nerves
cases.notes: Verified in Anatomy & Physiology 2e Ch 13.4 (p. 557-558, Fig 13.24).

cases.query: What are the anatomical boundaries and contents of the femoral triangle?
expected_answer_points: Superior border: inguinal ligament; lateral border: sartorius; medial border: adductor longus
Contents from lateral to medial (NAVEL): femoral nerve, femoral artery, femoral vein, lymphatics
Clinical relevance for femoral pulse palpation, vascular access, and femoral hernias
cases.notes: 2 chunks in Anatomy & Physiology 2e contain 'femoral triangle' (tests retrieval precision against spell-correction drift).

cases.query: Compare parathyroid hormone regulation and the diagnostic approach to primary hyperparathyroidism across internal medicine and endocrinology.
expected_answer_points: Elevated serum calcium with elevated or non-suppressed intact PTH confirms primary hyperparathyroidism
Exclude familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia (FHH) via 24-hour urine calcium / calcium-to-creatinine clearance ratio
Surgical parathyroidectomy is indicated for symptomatic patients or asymptomatic patients meeting age/renal/bone density thresholds
cases.notes: Tests explicit multi-book user selection sovereignty.

expected_answer_points: Strict scoping to the selected Cornea textbook (User Selection Sovereignty)
